summary: FINAL INDEPENDENT AUDIT of src/spine/{units,derive,assemble,compose}.py. I edited nothing. Every repro in x_spine's report was re-run on my own instruments; the numbers reproduce. FOUR of their seven claims are CONFIRMED_CORRECT, TWO hold but are NARROWER than written, and ONE new false statement is introduced by the very guard item 1 adds. THE HEADLINE: item 1's repair is real and I measured it from both sides -- floor gave (-3,-2,-2,-1,-1,-1,-1) at accum=4, HEAD's truncation gives (-2,-2,-1,-1,0,0,0), the working tree refuses every negative at accum in (1,2,4,8), positives are bit-identical (0,1,3->0; 4,7->1; 8->2; 52->13; 62->15; 1000 at accum=1 ->1000; 62 at accum=64 ->0), the only call site is opt/api.py:1496 in a function with no live caller, no `except TypeError` is on that path, and the suite is green. BUT THE MESSAGE THE NEW GUARD PRINTS CONTRADICTS THE FUNCTION'S OWN DOCSTRING: it says the fault 'was caught until 2026-09-04 only as a side effect of `//` flooring ..., which missed every deficit smaller than accum'. Flooring MISSED NOTHING -- floor(n/k) <= -1 for every n < 0, so at accum=4 deficits of 1, 2 and 3 all raised. It was the truncation repair that missed them, which is what the docstring twelve lines above says in as many words. This round set out to end false equations and printed a new false sentence inside the guard meant to end one; the same clause is queued for src/opt/api.py in x_spine's unfinished, so it will travel unless it is fixed first. SECOND: item 3's replacement blocker is right for OPT.build and WRONG for the other two sites. I neutralised CAP.startup_refusals and re-ran compose(): it does NOT then reach RUN.new_cadences or RUN.cadence_audit -- it stops at RUN.new_clock, compose.py:2108, ASSEMBLY_ORDER row 32, and RunClock.begin_epoch at :2116 (row 33) raises after that. So 'unreachable only because capacity/api.py::startup_refusals raises at row 29 ... SEVEN before RUN.cadence_audit' (compose.py:2316) and 'unreachable only because ... and this is row 35' (compose.py:2170) are both false as exclusives, and the ASSEMBLY_ORDER cadence row's 'THE EARLIER STUB IS CAP.startup_refusals AT ROW 29' names one of three. That is the same shape as the RUN.process_setup sentence they correctly refuted, one stub further along. THIRD: item 5 replaced a stale-number carrier with THREE FRESH NUMERIC CLAIMS THAT NO CHECK CAN SEE, in the one carrier that is auto-rendered into docs/03_WIRING.md. I ran tests/test_contract.py's own _K13_PATTERNS over the new sentence: only '23 declared couplings' matches. 'SIX cross-package edges', '19 of WIRE_BUDGET=25' and 'four ... intra-package' all escape -- and K13 HAS a '<n> intra-package' pattern and a '<n> cross-package wires' pattern that writing the digits would have hit. Items 2, 4 and 6 are confirmed to the measurement: I rebuilt all four of their O11 scratch trees and got A=PASS, B=FAIL(assemble.py:1020 only), C=FAIL(compose.py, exactly one finding), D=FAIL(4 on assemble.py + 1 on compose.py), plus a fifth tree proving C PASSES on the real tree; all 23 DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS entries read and the seven waits verified entry by entry; and item 6's proposed block executed verbatim prints ALL PROPOSED ASSERTIONS PASS. Isolated re-run on a clean HEAD carrying only their three spine files plus the regenerated doc: all green, so nothing depends on another owner's in-flight edits. INV-R2-1 is not in scope here (this is the spine, not the fabric) and I did not re-run it; I make no claim about the gradient path. Report written to /home/user/LLM-Test/.rework/audits/y_spine.json.

findings.detail: THE NEW GUARD PRINTS A SENTENCE THAT IS FALSE, AND THE SAME FUNCTION'S DOCSTRING SAYS THE OPPOSITE TWELVE LINES ABOVE. The raised message ends: 'This was caught until 2026-09-04 only as a side effect of `//` flooring a partial step up into a whole one, WHICH MISSED EVERY DEFICIT SMALLER THAN ACCUM; it is checked here now.' Flooring missed no such deficit. floor(n/k) is at most -1 for every n < 0, so under floor a deficit of 1, 2 or 3 at accum=4 each produced due=Steps(-1) against taken=Steps(0) and `due != taken` RAISED -- which is exactly the detection item 1 exists to restore, and exactly what the docstring at derive.py:568-577 states: 'every negative delta came back non-zero, opt/api.py::counters compared it against a `taken` of Steps(0) and raised', and then 'Correcting the rounding to truncation ... turned every deficit of 1 to k-1 backward passes into Steps(0) against Steps(0) and counters() said NOTHING.' The clause that missed those deficits was TRUNCATION, the earlier same-day repair, not flooring. So the file now holds two statements about one mechanism and the one a run will print is the wrong one -- the docstring/body disagreement item 1 closed, reopened one line lower as a docstring/MESSAGE disagreement. THE CLAUSE IS ALSO QUEUED TO TRAVEL: x_spine's unfinished item for src/opt/api.py::counters proposes the identical wording ('Until 2026-09-04 it was caught only as a side effect of `//` flooring a partial step up into a whole one, which missed every deficit smaller than accum and could be cancelled by a simultaneous step regression'), so landing that patch verbatim puts the false clause in a second file. The trailing half of that proposed sentence -- 'could be cancelled by a simultaneous step regression' -- IS true of floor (a resume losing 4 backward passes and one step at accum=4 gives due=Steps(-1) against taken=Steps(-1)) and should be kept. SECOND, SMALLER, IN THE SAME MESSAGE: derive.py:595 says 'The message below names the two counter keys instead'; the message names FOUR ('opt.ckpt.backward_at_load and opt.ckpt.step_at_load against opt.backward and opt.step'). The four keys all exist, so this is a count in prose, not a bad citation. Exact find/replace in unfinished.

Against the floor tree (git archive 2e8a63e~1): opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(-1),4) ;; '-1 steps', (-2) ;; '-1 steps', (-3) ;; '-1 steps' -- all three != Steps(0), so `due != taken` at opt/api.py:1499 fires on every deficit smaller than accum. Against HEAD 76c56ff: the same three ;; '0 steps','0 steps','0 steps' -- these are the ones that were missed. grep -n 'names the two counter keys' src/spine/derive.py ;; :595.

findings.detail: THE MISCOUNT IS GONE AND THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT TODAY, BUT THE FIX WRITES THREE FRESH UNCHECKABLE NUMERIC CLAIMS INTO THE ONE CARRIER THAT IS AUTO-PUBLISHED. Everything asserted is true as measured: tests/test_couplings.py C4 prints '23 coupling(s) resolved against 9 stand-in package(s); 19 wire(s) of 25 budgeted, 4 intra-package', src/spine/wire.py:54 sets WIRE_BUDGET = 25, assemble.build(environ={}) returns 13 configs and a Wires reading '19/25 wires, 6 emitting packages', so six cross-package edges remain; the three deferral reasons match DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS['WORLD.manage'] including the `latent` clause ('`latent` is real but arrives BACKWARDS: WORLD.loss_terms is a B row and this pass ran at A'); world/api.py::state_dict's docstring at :354-357 does say the loop-side plateau state '(_wl_ema, _wl_lastgrow) ... MOVES INSIDE THIS PACKAGE'; tools/render_wiring.py --check is clean at 239 lines. BUT docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3307-3312, in the very table that filed this carrier, states the rule the fix breaks: 'tests/test_couplings.py's C4 and spine/assemble.py::render print the live figures; ANY PROSE COPY IS ONE THAT CAN GO STALE IN SILENCE ... The count is not searched for by K13 -- its own output says "NOT SEARCHED FOR: a number written in words".' I ran tests/test_contract.py's own _K13_PATTERNS over the new sentence. Of its four numbers exactly ONE is checked -- '23 declared couplings', by the '<n> couplings / <n> coupling rows' pattern. 'one of the SIX cross-package edges that remain' is invisible because SIX is a word and the pattern wants '<n> cross-package WIRES'; 'four of the 23 declared couplings are intra-package' is invisible because four is a word, and K13 HAS a '<n> intra-package' pattern that '4 intra-package' would have hit; '19 of WIRE_BUDGET=25 are spent' is invisible because the budget/ledger pattern is `(\d+)\s+of\s+(?:a\s+)?(\d+)` and 'of WIRE_BUDGET=25' does not match. So three of the four live figures were copied into prose in the one place tools/render_wiring.py republishes verbatim, with nothing to catch them when the budget moves -- the failure mode this whole sweep is chasing, in the carrier the contract calls the worst-placed of the five. The remedy is to write the two word-numbers as digits so K13's existing patterns bite, and to point at C4 for the budget rather than copy it; exact find/replace in unfinished. Their two stale-description handoffs (src/capacity/levers.py:183 and docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3289) are correctly identified and both still read present-tense.

findings.detail: THE TWO FACTS THEIR REPAIR LEANS ON ARE TRUE, AND ONE THING IN THIS FILE IS NOT NOTHING. Confirmed: `class UnitError(TypeError)` at units.py:28, so the new refusal is not caught by any `except ValueError`; Clock.__init__ only int()s its argument, so a negative Backwards is constructible and the refusal has to be written in derive; counters() has no live caller. That is precisely the arithmetic the SAME ROUND'S new comment in the same file refuses by name at derive.py:663-665: 'Integer `//` and not `int(n / k)`: float division loses exactness above 2**53 and a backward count is unbounded.' Measured, not argued: flush_period(Steps(2**53+1), 1) returns 9007199254740992 where the exact answer is 9007199254740993, and flush_period(Steps(10**17+1), 3) returns 33333333333333332 where the exact answer is 33333333333333333. No live configuration reaches those magnitudes -- the cadences these carry are in the tens of thousands -- so this is low severity and I am not calling it a bug in a run; it is a rule the file states in one function and breaks in two others, which is exactly the class of disagreement item 1 was opened for. ONE MORE, IN A FILE NEITHER OF US OWNS BUT THAT CITES THIS ONE: tests/test_ownership.py:1602 and :1668 both cite 'units.py:86' as the home of 'There is no implicit path between kinds ... call the named function in spine.derive', and O11 PRINTS that citation in every finding it raises. units.py:86 is `__slots__ = ("n", "gates")`; the sentence is at units.py:160-162, inside Clock.convert.
